result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover line length, body size, line height, letter-spacing and paragraph/list spacing, and both give concrete CSS. A also says outright that h3 at 14px is barely larger than the 13px body text, and it explains how headings should group with the text below them. B fixes the heading sizes in its CSS but never names the size problem. B ranks the fixes more clearly, while A orders them only by list position and closes with a contrast note that slightly blurs the priorities. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers handle text size, line length, line height, block spacing and letter-spacing well, and both give concrete CSS. B is the only one to say outright that h3 at 14px is barely larger than the 13px body text, and it explains both the heading scale and the spacing that groups each heading with its text. A, by contrast, changes the heading sizes without explaining the problem. A ranks its fixes more clearly and stays in scope, while B ranks less and adds a note about color and contrast, though it doesn't actually change any colors.
